visual.text: Outgrown it? Someone else is about to grow into it.
Pass on your uniforms and textbooks. Pick up what you need for next year.

A long table in a school hall is piled with folded uniforms sorted by size. A tall Secondary 4 boy hands a stack of textbooks to a much smaller boy, who is grinning and already holding the top book open.

New uniforms and a full booklist are a heavy bill at the start of every year. Yet in most homes, last year’s books sit in a box, and shirts that no longer fit hang at the back of the wardrobe. Bring them to the Swap. Whatever you bring, someone will use — and whatever you need, you take home free.

visual.title: What we accept
items: School uniforms and PE attire, washed and without tears

questions.text: Look at the headline: ‘Outgrown it? Someone else is about to grow into it.’ What does it suggest about the things students no longer need?

scheme.answer: They are still useful, because a younger student will soon need exactly those things.
accept: Items that are too small or no longer needed by one student can be used by another, so they should not be wasted.

seeds.text: It suggests that these things are still useful because a younger student will need them soon.

It suggests that old things should be thrown away.
It suggests that students grow.
Someone else is about to grow into it.

questions.text: How does the picture support the message of the poster?

scheme.answer: It shows an older student passing his books to a younger one who is clearly delighted, which shows that used items are welcomed and put to use by someone else.
accept: The smaller boy’s grin shows that what one student no longer needs can make another student happy.

seeds.text: It shows an older boy giving his books to a younger boy who is very happy to get them, so we see that used things are still wanted by someone.
The small boy is grinning and already reading the book, which proves that things you have finished with can make another student glad.
It shows that the uniforms are sold at a cheap price in the hall.
It shows what the school hall looks like.
It shows that Secondary 4 boys are taller than other boys.

questions.text: ‘There is no need to bring something in order to take something. Nobody will ask.’ Why do you think the poster includes these lines?

scheme.answer: To assure students who have nothing to give that they can still take what they need without feeling embarrassed.
accept: So that families who need the items will come and take them freely, knowing that nobody will question or judge them.

seeds.text: To assure students who have nothing to give that they can still take things and need not feel embarrassed about it.

To show that nobody is interested in the Swap.
To tell students the rules of the Swap.
Because there is no need to bring something in order to take something.

questions.text: According to Aditi’s words, what advantage can a used textbook have over a new one?

scheme.answer: It may contain the previous owner’s notes, which help the next student understand the subject better.
accept: The notes written in it by an older student can explain the lessons more clearly.
